title: KVCache TTL amplification causing eviction starvation and transient cache blackholes
creator: Maya Santos
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-03-09 exposed a TTL amplification bug in the KV cache writeback/refresh path that caused sustained eviction starvation for hot namespaces. The symptom was a sudden drop in cache hit-rate for several large tenants followed by high latency due to increased backend fetches. This ticket contains the investigation notes, mitigations applied, and prioritized follow-up work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:04 UTC - Pager triggered: kv-cache tail latency > 2s for runtime-1 region-us-east-1. Multiple customer requests observed progressive cold-start behavior.
2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - Oncall (Liam) confirmed cache hit-rate drop from 92% -> 18% for affected shard set. Eviction rate remained low despite memory pressure.

2026-03-09 02:25 UTC - Emergency mitigation: enabled shard-level eviction throttle override and increased eviction aggressiveness for affected tenants (hotfix runtime toggle rev-2026-03-09-evict-override). Hit-rate recovered to 70% over 20 minutes.

2026-03-09 04:00 UTC - Initial triage concluded that many entries had unbounded extended TTLs due to a codepath that refreshed TTLs multiplicatively on read under heavy contention, causing 'TTL amplification'.
2026-03-10 - Postmortem investigation started; reproducer and unit tests added for TTL refresh semantics. Added checkpoints and new metrics for refresh-origin and refresh-factor.
2026-03-12 - Hotfix merged: cap refresh factor to 1.0 and introduced per-tenant max-refresh window. Deployed to runtime-1 and verified no regression in hit-rate across canary tenants.
2026-03-14 - Rolling follow-ups prioritized and assigned. This ticket opened to track complete remediation and observability improvements.
steps_to_reproduce: Set up a kv-cache shard with synthetic workload: 10k keys with skewed access (80/20 hot key distribution) and short base TTL (30s).
Enable read-refresh path that multiplies TTL by factor when key is read concurrently (mirrors production refresh behavior).
Drive sudden ramp of read QPS to hot keys using 200 concurrent clients for 15 minutes.

Observe that refresh factor multiplies TTL on every concurrent refresh leading to very large TTLs and lower eviction pressure; eviction thread sees low candidate churn and stops evicting leading to memory working set growth and cold misses for other namespaces.
root_cause: A refresh-on-read optimization multiplied an entry's TTL by a configurable factor on each concurrent access without adequately bounding the cumulative effect.

Under heavy concurrent reads the multiplicative refresh caused a small set of entries to acquire extremely long TTLs (TTL amplification), which prevented normal eviction cycles from selecting them as candidates.
Eviction heuristics relied on observed TTL and access recency; the amplified TTLs biased the eviction scorer, causing eviction starvation for other hot namespaces.
Insufficient telemetry: we lacked a metric that attributed refresh events to origin (read vs background-refresh) and lacked histograms of refresh-factor distribution across namespaces.
short_term_mitigation: Hotfix (deployed 2026-03-12): cap per-refresh multiplier to 1.0 and add a global guard that rejects refresh if resulting TTL exceeds baseTTL * 8.
Eviction policy tweak: temporarily increase eviction aggressiveness and add fallback that enforces minimum candidate churn per shard to avoid starvation.
Operational checklist: added a runbook step to toggle the hotfix flag and to scale eviction aggressiveness if hit-rate drops > 25% in a 5m window.
Customer comms: notified affected tenants via account success; flagged as P1 and offered support for manual cache warmup if needed.
long_term_remediation: Redesign refresh semantics: change multiplicative refresh to a capped additive model and introduce 'refresh-origin' tagging so we can distinguish user-initiated vs system refreshes.
Eviction scoring rewrite: add a TTL-saturation penalty that prevents extremely long-ttl entries from permanently shielding a shard from eviction candidates.
Comprehensive telemetry: emit per-refresh metrics (origin, factor, resultingTTL), per-tenant eviction-candidate-rate, and per-shard min-candidate threshold alerts.
Automated chaos test: add a load test in CI that simulates TTL amplification scenarios and asserts eviction fairness and bounded memory growth.
Backward compatibility: add a migration plan for older runtime clients that relied on multiplicative refresh; provide a compatibility flag for a deprecation period.

notes: We intentionally biased short-term remediation toward operational safety (cap + eviction tweak) to prevent recurrence during the rollout window.
Design-level changes will need cross-team signoff from Runtime, SRE, and Observability because eviction scoring touches global performance characteristics.
Estimate and deadlines assume no large regressions in p95 latency from the additive refresh; if CI shows regressions we'll need to re-evaluate schedule.
